findings.reason: The protected SQL solution selects customer_id from Customers WHERE year = 2021 AND revenue > 0. The single-table filter is canonical, optimal, and concise; no candidate is required.

WHERE year = 2021 AND revenue > 0 filters for rows matching the exact target year with strictly positive revenue. Because (customer_id, year) is unique, each customer produces at most one 2021 row without duplicates.
Scanning r customer rows takes O(r) time and O(o) output space for o qualifying customer IDs. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Outputs single column customer_id, excludes 0 or negative 2021 revenue, and ignores positive revenue from other years.

The approach accurately details single-pass row filtering for year = 2021 and revenue > 0, uniqueness guarantees, and relational complexity bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover positive-revenue-only filters, year-only filters, grouping/summing errors, self-joins, zero revenue, negative revenue, other year revenues, and empty outputs.
